title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1968-10-13

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1968 show with smoking Dark Star, Eleven and The Other One.
ai_review.review: The Charlie Miller/ Michael Owen soundboard release delivers crystal‑clear original 1968 mix, letting the band’s fire shine through. Highlights include a near‑perfect Dark Star, an incendiary Eleven, and a transcendent The Other One, while the second set is a bit uneven with a weaker New Potato transition. Overall the performance is tight, dynamic, and highly recommended for any 1968 Dead collection.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews are overwhelmingly positive (mostly 5‑star) praising both the musical performance and the pristine soundboard recording; only minor set‑list hiccups noted, leading to a top‑tier combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, original 1968 mix praised as “original sound” and given five stars for mix and recording; no reported dropouts or muffiness.

poor_songs: New Potato (average, abrupt splice into Drums)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set strong and cohesive; second set a little uneven but still contains high points like The Other One and the Eleven transition. Some listeners prefer St. Stephen→Eleven over St. Stephen→Not Fade Away.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Top‑notch guitar work, especially on Dark Star and Death Don't Have No Mercy; described as masterful and feeding off the band.
band_member_comments.Phil: Powerful bass playing, “feeding off” the drummers; praised for tight interplay.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drummers described as fabulous and tight, though the Drums segment after New Potato was noted as less interesting.
